audit_status.source_base: Hebrew 2 Kings / Melakhim Bet Athaliah, Joash rescue, temple coup, coronation, and execution narrative, draft aligned later
audit_status.review_note: First-pass draft reviewed for royal-child massacre, Jehosheba's rescue, six-year concealment, Jehoiada's armed temple plan, covenant and coronation, Athaliah's protest, execution outside sanctuary, Baal-temple destruction, priest killing, and transfer of the child king to palace.

verses.restored: Athaliah mother of Ahaziah saw that her son was dead, and she rose and destroyed all seed of kingdom.

But Jehosheba daughter of king Joram, sister of Ahaziah, took Joash son of Ahaziah and stole him from among king's sons being put to death, him and his nurse in bedchamber; they hid him from Athaliah, and he was not put to death.
He was with her hidden in house of YHWH six years, while Athaliah reigned over land.

In seventh year Jehoiada sent and took commanders of hundreds of Carites and runners and brought them to him in house of YHWH. He cut covenant with them, made them swear in house of YHWH, and showed them king's son.
He commanded them, saying, This is thing you shall do: one third of you who enter on Sabbath shall keep watch of king's house,
one third at gate Sur, and one third at gate behind runners; you shall keep watch of house in alternation.
Two divisions of you, all who go out on Sabbath, shall keep watch of house of YHWH around king.
You shall surround king, each man with weapons in hand; one who comes within ranks shall be put to death. Be with king when he goes out and when he comes in.
Commanders of hundreds did according to all Jehoiada the priest commanded. Each took his men entering on Sabbath and going out on Sabbath and came to Jehoiada the priest.
The priest gave commanders of hundreds spears and shields that belonged to king David, which were in house of YHWH.
Runners stood, each man with weapons in hand, from right side of house to left side of house, by altar and house, around king.
He brought out king's son, put crown upon him and testimony, and they made him king and anointed him; they clapped hands and said, Let king live!
Athaliah heard voice of runners and people and came to people at house of YHWH.

She looked, and behold, king standing by pillar according to custom, commanders and trumpets beside king, and all people of land rejoicing and blowing trumpets. Athaliah tore her garments and cried, Conspiracy! Conspiracy!

Jehoiada the priest commanded commanders of hundreds, officers of army, and said to them, Bring her out between ranks, and whoever goes after her put to death by sword; for priest had said, Let her not be put to death in house of YHWH.
They laid hands upon her, and she went by way of horses' entrance to king's house, and there she was put to death.
Jehoiada cut covenant between YHWH and king and people, to be people of YHWH, and between king and people.

All people of land came to house of Baal and tore it down; its altars and images they broke thoroughly, and Mattan priest of Baal they killed before altars. The priest appointed overseers over house of YHWH.
He took commanders of hundreds, Carites, runners, and all people of land; they brought king down from house of YHWH and came by way of gate of runners to king's house. He sat upon throne of kings.
All people of land rejoiced, and city was quiet; Athaliah they had put to death by sword at king's house.
Joash was seven years old when he became king.

translation_notes: Athaliah is blamed for destroying the royal seed, but her portrayal comes through a hostile dynastic narrative. Her actions remain murderous without turning her into a misogynistic archetype of female rule.
Jehosheba and the nurse save Joash from a royal-child massacre. Their courage and caregiving are central to the survival story.
Joash is concealed in the temple for six years and crowned at seven. A child king remains a child subject to adult agendas, not proof that youth can safely carry sovereign power.
Jehoiada organizes an armed coup inside sacred space, including a lethal perimeter around the child. Temple authority does not automatically legitimate political violence.
Athaliah cries 'conspiracy' accurately: a coup is underway, even if the narrative supports it.
She is executed outside the temple to avoid sanctuary pollution; relocation of execution does not create due process.
The destruction of Baal's temple and killing of Mattan are religious violence and must never authorize attacks on other faith communities.
Covenant between YHWH, king, and people should not be used to fuse religion and state into theocracy or leader immunity.
Public joy and city quiet after a coup report the winners' perspective and do not erase the dead, frightened, or politically silenced.
safety_note: Do not use 2 Kings 11 to justify child rulers, palace massacres, armed temple coups, execution without trial, misogyny toward women in power, theocracy, religious-site destruction, or killing clergy of another tradition. Center Jehosheba's rescue, the child's vulnerability, and the difference between dynastic success and ethical justice.
